title: Bloom at the Intake
briefing: A warm reservoir has developed an algal bloom near a drinking-water intake. Laboratory confirmation will arrive after the next pumping cycle.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: The deep intake is clean in the last sample, but its older pumps cannot sustain normal pressure at every elevation.
private_intelligence.community: Hill districts already store water in shared tanks; another restriction may be seen as preferential treatment elsewhere.
private_intelligence.economy: Food processors can suspend one cycle if compensation is paid promptly; small laundries cannot afford a similar shutdown.
private_intelligence.safety: Boiling will not remove every possible toxin, so a generic boil-water notice could create false reassurance.

choices.title: Switch Intakes
choices.description: Use the deep intake and limit nonessential demand.
choices.consequence: Cleaner intake water reduces exposure, but low pressure and business curtailment burden the higher districts.

choices.title: Buy Treatment Time
choices.description: Purchase emergency filtration and maintain a restricted supply.
choices.consequence: Emergency filters preserve pressure and public access, but fast procurement consumes reserves and needs technical supervision.

choices.title: Pause and Test
choices.description: Stop reservoir distribution until sampling is complete.
choices.consequence: A clear precaution builds confidence and avoids uncertain exposure, while interrupted supply damages service and commerce.
